source: Cok, Motte, Hmina, El Hassani, Demsar, Tavcar, Vukasinovic (2026) Evaluating TRIZ with and without LLM support (PDS 2026), design and sample
finding: Gap 10. Between-subjects experiment: 2 methods (contradiction matrix alone, TRIZ-C, vs matrix plus LLM, TRIZ-C+LLM) by 3 problems. Each student solved one problem with one method, assigned at random.
numbers: N=113 analysed (TRIZ-C+LLM 62, TRIZ-C 51); one student excluded for not understanding the problem. Problems: polymer gear test rig (GT), mounting bracket (MB), wind turbine power (WT). Design quality = 4 criteria (feasibility, requirements, innovativeness, elaboration) on 7-point scales, rated by PhD-level experts and averaged.
limits: Read through a page-fetch summary; Table 1 and Table 2 cell counts and means were not in the text. Per-cell n unknown. LLM model and prompting skill were not controlled.
agent_relevance: Closes the N and statistics question left open for K17.

source: Cok, Motte, Hmina, El Hassani, Demsar, Tavcar, Vukasinovic (2026) Evaluating TRIZ with and without LLM support (PDS 2026), design quality results
finding: LLM help did not raise design quality overall. The gain appeared in one of three problems only, and that group was AI-specialised.
numbers: Method main effect F(1,108)=3.21, p=.076. Problem F(2,108)=27.89, p<.001. Method x Problem F(2,108)=7.58, p=.001. Simple effects: GT F=.51 p=.479; MB F=.06 p=.809; WT F(1,108)=34.67 p<.001 (higher with LLM). Levene test p=.018 (unequal variances). Effect sizes for quality not reported.
limits: Only one of three simple effects is significant; the WT group had AI-specialised students (authors' own caveat), so prompting skill and problem are confounded. Self-rated innovation gain, idea quality and feasibility: p=.321, .099, .945.
agent_relevance: Skill with the tool may matter more than the tool. An agent that always applies the step has no skill gap, but it should not expect a gain on every task.

source: Cok, Motte, Hmina, El Hassani, Demsar, Tavcar, Vukasinovic (2026) Evaluating TRIZ with and without LLM support (PDS 2026), workload and time
finding: The LLM made the TRIZ steps feel easier but did not change satisfaction, usefulness or willingness to reuse.
numbers: Difficulty of defining the contradiction t(111)=-4.123, p<.001, d=-0.779. Overall problem difficulty t(111)=-3.784, p<.001, d=-0.715. Completion time 40.3 min (SD 20.9) with LLM vs 46.2 min (SD 21.3) without; no p reported. Usefulness p=.133, reuse p=.541, time sufficiency p=.307. Mental effort: interaction F(1,88)=6.89, p=.048, only the WT simple effect significant.
limits: Self-report. The contradiction step is where the LLM helped most in felt effort, which fits the machine results that contradiction naming is the weak step (Trapp, TRIZBench).
agent_relevance: Supports using the model to name contradictions, but not a claim that this raises outcome quality.

source: Szczepanik and Chudziak (2025) TRIZ Agents: multi-agent LLM approach, token cost and no single-agent control
finding: Gap 9 and gap 6. A manager plus specialist agents (GPT, web search, RAG on TRIZ) ran the six TRIZ steps on one gantry crane case. The paper has no single-agent control and no token-matched comparison, and says it does not compare architectures.
numbers: One run cost 60 to 80 graph calls and 150,000 to 250,000 tokens. Two runs assessed by hand against the published case. Engineering contradictions named differently from the paper (Speed vs Stability, Load capacity vs Safety). Physical contradictions matched exactly. Only one inventive principle matched. The matrix lookup is deterministic code, so it was not scored.
quote: The experiments follow the ideation process of agents solving the case study problem
limits: N=1 case, 2 runs, hand-assessed, no novelty rating. Manager never sent work back for revision (authors list this as a severe limit). The TRIZ specialist rarely called its RAG tool.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 stays open. A 150k to 250k token cost per problem is the only cost figure found for TRIZ agents. Matches the schema warning that manager-plus-specialist layouts add cost without a measured gain.

source: Lee, Jeong, Yoo, Yang, Kang (2026) TRIZ-inspired text-to-CAD framework (Claude Sonnet 4.5)
finding: Gap 1, closest modern-model test. Same model, same chair CAD script, two prompts: a vanilla 'make it lighter' prompt versus a prompt carrying the strength-weight contradiction and a named inventive principle. Vanilla scaled dimensions down. TRIZ prompts changed structure.
numbers: One chair, FEA at 900 N. Vanilla: mass -31.8%, stress +64.1%, displacement +99.4%. Four TRIZ variants (principles 1, 8, 15, 40): mass -14.7%, -5.9%, -4.0%, -10.0% (mean 8.7%); stress -0.1%, +21.6%, +33.2%, +40.7%; displacement up to +44.4%.
quote: vanilla prompt drives the LLM toward quantitative scaling without structural reasoning
limits: N=1 design, one run per prompt, no replicates, no novelty or diversity rating, no rater. It measures structural trade-off, not creativity. The vanilla prompt was a one-line instruction, so the contrast mixes TRIZ content with prompt detail. Authors say run-to-run code differed in style but not in function.
agent_relevance: Shows the mechanism: a named contradiction pushes the model off a quantitative-scaling default. Not evidence of blind-rated novelty at equal tokens.

source: Liu, Huang, Wang (2026) TRIZa: guiding agent evolution from pattern recognition to solution invention
finding: Gap 1 and gap 2. An evolutionary search where each mutation must instantiate a chosen TRIZ principle and its matrix entry. Reruns of candidate and baseline under one protocol beat baselines on three cybersecurity tasks. The authors state they cannot tell whether TRIZ guidance caused the gains.
numbers: Formal CICIoT2023 V2: macro-F1 0.8325 to 0.8483 (+0.0158, +1.90% relative); attack recall +0.018; detector FPR -0.0017; 43 of 45 family-seed groups improved; all 5 seed blocks positive. The candidate failed two promotion thresholds (needed relative gain 3.2277% and FPR drop 0.005) and was withheld.
quote: do not identify which part of the workflow caused the improvements
limits: No ablation against untyped mutation. Domain is classifier tuning, not design ideation. Single author group. The study measures score, not novelty.
agent_relevance: Clean statement of what is missing: nobody has run typed-TRIZ mutation against untyped mutation at equal budget. Its promotion gate (reject a gain that comes with a worse harm) matches schema guardrail style.

source: Xu, Wu, Zhao (2026) TRIZ-RAGNER: retrieval-augmented LLM for TRIZ-aware NER in patents
finding: Gap 2 and gap 3. Retrieval of TRIZ parameter definitions plus reranking plus a structured prompt lifts contradiction-pair extraction over plain GPT. Ablation shows each part matters.
numbers: PaTRIZ data. BiLSTM-CRF F1 60.7, BERT-CRF 68.5, RoBERTa-CRF 71.7, GPT zero-shot 73.7, GPT + prompt engineering 76.9, TRIZ-RAGNER 84.2 (P 85.6, R 82.9). Ablation F1: no retrieval 78.1, no rerank 79.8, no structured prompt 76.6.
limits: Low confidence. The text contains an unrelated paragraph about digital twins and reinforcement learning (stray 'SR-DTMA' text), no sample count, no seeds, no variance. Parameter-level F1 on a patent set, not ideation. Treat as weak.
agent_relevance: If trusted, grounding in a fixed TRIZ parameter list helps naming, which agrees with TRIZBench and AutoTRIZ. The quality flags mean it cannot carry a claim alone.

source: Wang and Uzzi (2026) TRIZBench, contradiction detection with abstention
finding: Gap 3. Prompts told models to abstain when a contradiction could not be grounded, and no_case segments served as negatives. Detection F1 was still only moderate for zero/few-shot and rose with LoRA fine-tuning.
numbers: Case-level HasF1: Qwen3-8B 0.84 ZS / 0.87 FS; Qwen3-32B 0.76 / 0.75; LLaMA3.1-8B 0.77 / 0.83; LLaMA3.1-70B 0.80 / 0.76; Gemini-2.5-Pro 0.77 / 0.82; LoRA Qwen3-8B 0.90, LLaMA3.1-8B 0.88. Few-shot gains small and sometimes negative. PairF1 0.29 to 0.45.
limits: Abstain is in the prompt for every arm, so there is no arm without abstain: its own effect is not isolated. Labels partly made by Gemini-2.5-Pro, so the Gemini rows may be favoured. False-positive rate is not reported separately.
agent_relevance: An abstain instruction alone leaves F1 around 0.75 to 0.87, so a second pass or a code check is still needed. Few-shot examples are not a reliable fix.

source: Trapp and Warschat (2024) LLM-based extraction of contradictions from patents, test on contradiction-free patents
finding: Gap 3. On 100 patents that annotators labelled contradiction-free, GPT-4 still extracted a contradiction from 86. The authors do not conclude the model is wrong: they show a golf-ball patent where the label itself looks mistaken.
numbers: 86 of 100 flagged (87 contradictions, one patent had 2); mean 4.84 extracted sentences vs 5.88 in patents with contradictions. On the contradiction set: recall 0.71, 3.19 false-positive sentences per patent. PaTRIZ fine-tuned BERT precision 0.33.
quote: One possible explanation for the discrepancy to the PaGAN annotations is that GPT-4 is not good at distinguishing
limits: Single prompt, single model (gpt-4-1106-preview), no abstain option tested, no second pass tested. Ground truth uncertain, so the 86% is an upper bound on hallucination.
agent_relevance: The false-claim rate cannot be read as 86% error. It does show that a contradiction step with no 'none' route will almost always report one. The schema needs an explicit none-found exit and an independent check.

source: Jiang, Li, Qian, Zhang, Luo (2025) AutoTRIZ, design of the lookup step and diversity choice
finding: Gap 2 and gap 6. The LLM only names the contradiction (two of 39 parameters). Principle lookup is code: a function call into the contradiction matrix returns only the principles listed for that cell. The system deliberately resolves one contradiction per run and keeps the randomness to widen the idea set.
numbers: Contradiction may differ per run; 100 runs per case used to show spread (earlier numbers: 7 of 10 cases match or half-match textbook). No non-TRIZ baseline, no token or time cost, no rater study. Authors call the lack of an objective evaluation of solutions a limitation.
quote: there is no objective mechanism to evaluate the effectiveness of generated solutions
limits: All evaluation is against textbook cases the model may have seen, plus one battery case checked by a co-author. Authors' own tool.
agent_relevance: Supports a code-fixed lookup with the model confined to the naming step. No test shows the LLM adding anything when it picks principles freely, beyond TRIZBench's rerank result (d11).

source: Wang and Uzzi (2026) TRIZBench, principle prediction baselines
finding: Gap 2. Non-LLM lookup nearly equals the best LLM method. The LLM adds a small gain when it reranks matrix candidates, and does worse when it generates freely.
numbers: Hit@3 case / patent: matrix lookup 0.67 / 0.48; TF-IDF 0.69 / 0.56; Qwen3-8B ZS 0.39 / 0.27; Gemini ZS 0.45 / 0.31; Matrix-Rerank up to 0.71 / 0.59. Authors: direct LLM prompting underperforms; LLMs work best as selectors over matrix-consistent candidates.
limits: Labels are the principles the source inventors used, not the best principles. Hit@3 rewards recall of a known set, not novelty. Rerank gain over TF-IDF is about 0.02 to 0.03.
agent_relevance: Answers gap 2: lookup is as good as free choice on this benchmark, and the model's extra value is small reranking. Put the lookup in code.

source: Chen, Tsang, Jing, Sun (2024) LLM-augmented morphological analysis approach for conceptual design (DRS 2024)
finding: Gap 4 neighbour. Three stages (decomposition, generation, combination) plus feedback. Abstract says concept quality improved, cognitive load fell, interaction was more engaging.
numbers: No numbers: N, conditions and statistics are not on the abstract page. Full PDF was blocked (HTTP 403).
limits: Abstract only; opened:false because the paper itself was not read. An earlier note of a three-arm design came from a secondary summary and is unverified.
agent_relevance: Still the closest LLM study to the function-and-morphology half. It does not test a task-questioning step.

source: Owen and Roberts (2024) Design contradictions: help or hindrance? (poster)
finding: Poster, no experiment. Argues that LLMs tend toward similar outputs and handle contradictory design words (the example is a round bar chart) badly. Says new methods are needed.
numbers: No N, no scores. One worked example.
limits: Opinion poster in visualisation design. Do not cite as evidence. Not about TRIZ contradictions in the engineering sense.
agent_relevance: Flags a risk: a contradictory prompt can yield an output that satisfies neither side. Untested.

source: Hernandez, Schmidt, Okudan Kremer (2012), Ogot and Okudan (2006), Dumas 2016, Chang 2016, Dumas and Schmidt 2015 (re-read side by side for gap 7)
finding: Gap 7. Reading the numbers side by side, the sign of the quantity effect seems to follow training length, unit of count and what was counted. This is a pattern in the table, not a tested explanation.
numbers: Ogot: a full course on the matrix, per team, feasible concepts, 8.94 vs 4.42. Hernandez: one lecture, quantity p=.2879, .5409, .6291 (n.s.). Dumas 2016: 50 minute lecture, fluency -19.3%, N=44. Dumas and Schmidt 2015: 6 week course, novelty +30.8%, N=19. TRIZ10: 30 minute lecture, ideas +178%, N=13, no control.
limits: Mix of firsthand (Hernandez, Ogot, opened in earlier passes) and second-hand (Dumas, Chang) numbers. The original Dumas and Chang papers were not opened (paywalled). Quasi-randomised designs confound everything.
agent_relevance: For an agent, training length does not apply, so human quantity losses may not transfer. What may transfer is that a forced structure can narrow search early. Untested.

source: Valentine, Belski, Hamilton (2017) and Belski et al. (2014, 2015), Simple ideation (retry of access)
finding: Gap 7 support. The host server refused connections (ECONNREFUSED) on the fetches, so the earlier snippet-level numbers stay unverified.
numbers: Earlier snippet figures, unverified: control 5.03, pen-and-paper 5.04, computer 4.20 distinct ideas per person.
limits: Not opened. Left at snippet level.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on K06 numbers beyond 'one gain, one null'.

source: Fiorineschi, Frillici, Rotini (2018) Exploiting TRIZ tools for enhancing systematic conceptual design activities (J. Eng. Design) and Computers in Industry review
finding: Gaps 4 and 5. Both publisher pages were not reachable (HTTP 403 and an empty redirect), so I could not check whether the Problem-Solution Network was tested with participants. No other source found describes such a test.
limits: Paywalled. Absence of a test is inferred from the searches in earlier passes (K20), not from these pages.
agent_relevance: Gaps 4 and 5 stay open and are an experiment to run on the agent.

source: arXiv listing search for TRIZ with LLM, run 2026-11-19
finding: Gap 8 and coverage. The arXiv list for 'TRIZ LLM' returned 8 papers: AutoTRIZ, TRIZ-GPT, Trapp and Warschat, TRIZ Agents, TRIZ-RAGNER, text-to-CAD, TRIZa, and one unrelated enterprise-AI paper (2409.17408, E-GenAI, not a TRIZ test). Other searches (SCAMPER LLM, design heuristics LLM, morphological LLM, multi-agent token-matched creativity) returned nothing relevant.
numbers: 8 hits, 7 relevant, 0 with blind-rated novelty from independent raters on post-cutoff problems.
limits: arXiv only; Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex and the arXiv API were rate-limited and the WebSearch budget was spent. Journal-only work could be missed.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 remains open: no study with independent raters, kappa, and post-cutoff problems.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT, post-cutoff robustness (from earlier evidence a15, c06)
finding: Gap 8. The only post-cutoff signal is TRIZ-GPT recall 0.544 vs 0.400 on later cases, across different collections; AutoTRIZ's cases come from textbooks.
numbers: Recall 0.544 vs 0.400 (from the earlier read of arXiv 2408.05897; not re-opened for this line).
limits: Not re-opened. Not a clean test.

source: Mohammadi and Zeng (2025) rater details re-checked from earlier evidence c12 and c13
finding: Gap 8. Ratings came from two graduate evaluators (accuracy) and Shah-style counts; no kappa reported in the lines recorded.
numbers: Two evaluators; 3 cases; ideas 20 vs 4, 7 vs 2, 18 vs 1 or 2.
limits: Not re-opened. Evaluators were not independent of the group.
